title: Your first budget in 20 minutes
description: No spreadsheets required — a friendly first budget you can make on one sheet of paper.

body.heading: Start with what comes in
paragraphs: Write down the money you actually receive in a typical month — from work, family, or other regular sources. Use the amount that really arrives, not a hoped-for amount. If it changes month to month, use a low, realistic figure.

Next, list what must go out: transport, food basics, phone, school costs, and anything you are committed to paying. Be honest rather than optimistic; a budget built on real numbers is one you can trust.

body.heading: Give the rest a job
paragraphs: Whatever is left is your flexible money. Decide in advance how much goes to saving, how much to fun, and how much stays as a buffer for surprises. Even rough amounts are better than no plan.
Keep it visible for the first month — on your phone or a note on your desk. Check once a week whether reality matches the plan, and adjust kindly instead of giving up.

body.heading: A budget is a draft
paragraphs: Your first budget will not be perfect, and it does not need to be. Each month you learn something — a cost you forgot, a habit you want to change — and the next draft gets better.

takeaway: A first budget is just three lists: what comes in, what must go out, and a job for the rest.
